# Rapid Grant Proposal — Halcyon Threshold
Applicant: Morgan Hale
Email: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org
Project title: Independent Replication & Documentation of Agent Autonomy Evals
Amount requested: $12,000

## Summary
A small, time-limited team will independently replicate two published evaluations of agents operating with broad autonomy, produce clean reproducible notebooks, and publish a short public report highlighting where results are fragile or where documentation is missing. Outputs directly address the commonly cited gap of independent replication of safety results and evaluations of agents with broad autonomy, identified in the AI Safety Directory.

## Why me / Halcyon Threshold
Halcyon Threshold is a personal effort to contribute meaningfully to a good outcome for superintelligent AI. I have evenings/weekends availability, decent writing, okay Python, and a network of practitioners met via local meetup. This project is narrow, concrete, and deliverable in ~10 weeks.

## Plan
Week 1-2: Select two evaluations from 2025-2026 that have public artifacts but limited external validation. Confirm reproducibility feasibility with Sam Whitlock, indie evals person.
Week 3-7: Run replications on modest cloud compute. Document environment, prompts, seeds, and failure modes.
Week 8-9: Internal write-up, sanity checks with Priya Raman for data analysis review.
Week 10: Publish report and notebooks under CC-BY, submit summary to Alignment Commons.

## Budget
Compute: $3,500
Part-time data review (Priya Raman, 20h @ $40/h): $800
Reserve for incidental costs / open publication: $1,200
Project buffer / contingency: $6,500

Total: $12,000

## Risks & mitigations
Risk: Evaluations rely on proprietary models. Mitigation: choose evaluations with documented API access or open weights.
Risk: Limited time. Mitigation: narrow scope to two evaluations, fixed timeline.

## Deliverables
- Two reproducible replication notebooks
- 6-10 page public report with lessons
- Submission to Alignment Commons forum

Contact: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

args.subject: Can I pick your brain / ask for a few hours help?
args.body:
Hi Priya,

Great to meet at the meetup, and thanks for offering to help.

I’m putting together a small concrete project under Halcyon Threshold: independent replication and documentation of two agent autonomy evaluations, with a short public report. It’s narrow, 10 weeks, evenings/weekends.

Would you be open to a quick chat next week about whether this sounds useful and if you’d want to be involved for data review? I’m thinking ~20 hours total, and if we get a small grant I can compensate at a reasonable rate.

No pressure at all — I really appreciate the offer.

Best,
Morgan

args.subject: Replication project — could use your evals experience
args.body:
Hi Sam,

We met at the meetup a couple weeks ago. I’m Morgan, Halcyon Threshold.

I’m planning a small replication effort: pick two published agent autonomy evaluations from 2025-2026 and independently re-run them with clean notebooks and public documentation. Goal is to surface where results are fragile or under-documented.

Would you be open to a short conversation about which evaluations are actually replicable and worth the effort? I value your experience with indie evals and don’t want to waste time on a dead end.

Happy to work around your schedule.

Thanks,
Morgan

args.subject: Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?
args.body:
Hi Tessa,

Thanks for reaching out. I’m not comfortable commenting on record at this time — I work at Dorrance Logistics and my outside activities disclosure process isn’t complete yet, and I’d rather not be quoted publicly until that’s sorted.

Happy to revisit later.

Best,
Morgan Hale

args.subject: Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs
args.body:
Dear Corvid Institute,

Thank you for the invitation to sign the open letter on frontier training runs.

I am not signing at this time. I’m still navigating workplace disclosure constraints and want to keep my public affiliations minimal until I’ve spoken to HR.

I appreciate the work you’re doing and wish you the best with the letter.

Best regards,
Morgan Hale
Halcyon Threshold
